learning_outcomes.text: Understand the tasks of purchasing and the importance of material costs, including the difference between price and cost, as well as the short-term and long-term challenges of procurement.
Explain procurement goals and strategies, identify conflicts in goal systems, and classify product, sourcing, and supplier strategies.
Apply procurement analysis methods, especially Make or Buy analyses, ABC and XYZ analyses, and the creation of requirement specifications and functional specifications.
Systematically evaluate procurement markets and suppliers, collect information on market structures, narrow down suppliers, and build qualified supplier pools.
Professionally conduct procurement processes, including inquiry management, competitive bidding, global sourcing, offer processing, contract management, and price structure analysis.
Use negotiation and innovation skills in purchasing, conduct negotiations in role-plays, understand the importance of supplier innovations, and utilize insights into e-procurement.

For dual students: Dual students are encouraged to choose a topic from their respective partner company for the study work. This also enables them to acquire the competence to transfer the learned methods into the context of their partner company.

syllabus_topics: Procurement Tasks along the Product Development Process

assessment_methods.method: Study work with colloquium (written elaboration, presentation, oral examination)
